Simple, right? 75 76 ### No Handler, no Formatter, no Filter: one function to rule them all 77 78 How to add a handler? How to set up logs formatting? How to filter messages? How to set level? 79 80 One answer: the [`add()`](https://loguru.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/logger.html#loguru._logger.Logger.add) function. 81 82 ```python 83 logger.add(sys.stderr, format="{time} {level} {message}", filter="my_module", level="INFO") 84 ``` 85 86 This function should be used to register [sinks](https://loguru.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/logger.html#sink) which are responsible for managing [log messages](https://loguru.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/logger.html#message) contextualized with a [record dict](https://loguru.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/logger.html#record). A sink can take many forms: a simple function, a string path, a file-like object, a coroutine function or a built-in Handler. 87 88 Note that you may also [`remove()`](https://loguru.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/logger.html#loguru._logger.Logger.remove) a previously added handler by using the identifier returned while adding it. This is particularly useful if you want to supersede the default `stderr` handler: just call `logger.remove()` to make a fresh start. 89 90 ### Easier file logging with rotation / retention / compression 91 92 If you want to send logged messages to a file, you just have to use a string path as the sink. It can be automatically timed too for convenience: 93 94 ```python 95 logger.add("file_{time}.log") 96 ``` 97 98 It is also [easily configurable](https://loguru.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/logger.html#file) if you need rotating logger, if you want to remove older logs, or if you wish to compress your files at closure. 99 100 ```python 101 logger.add("file_1.log", rotation="500 MB") # Automatically rotate too big file 102 logger.add("file_2.log", rotation="12:00") # New file is created each day at noon 103 logger.add("file_3.log", rotation="1 week") # Once the file is too old, it's rotated 104 105 logger.add("file_X.log", retention="10 days") # Cleanup after some time 106 107 logger.add("file_Y.log", compression="zip") # Save some loved space 108 ``` 109 110 ### Modern string formatting using braces style 111 112 Loguru favors the much more elegant and powerful `{}` formatting over `%`, logging functions are actually equivalent to `str.format()`. 113 114 ```python 115 logger.info("If you're using Python {}, prefer {feature} of course!", 3.6, feature="f-strings") 116 ``` 117 118 ### Exceptions catching within threads or main 119 120 Have you ever seen your program crashing unexpectedly without seeing anything in the log file? This can be solved using the [`catch()`](https://loguru.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/logger.html#loguru._logger.Logger.catch) decorator / context manager which ensures that any error is correctly propagated to the [`logger`](https://loguru.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/logger.html#loguru._logger.Logger). 121 122 ```python 123 @logger.catch 124 def my_function(x, y, z): 125 # An error? It's caught anyway! 126 return 1 / (x + y + z) 127 ``` 128 129 ### Pretty logging with colors 130 131 Loguru automatically adds colors to your logs if your terminal is compatible. You can define your favorite style by using [markup tags](https://loguru.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/logger.html#color) in the sink format. 132 133 ```python 134 logger.add(sys.stdout, colorize=True, format="{time} {message}") 135 ``` 136 137 ### Asynchronous, Thread-safe, Multiprocess-safe 138 139 All sinks added to the [`logger`](https://loguru.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/logger.html#loguru._logger.Logger) are thread-safe by default. They are not multiprocess-safe, but you can `enqueue` the messages to ensure logs integrity. This same argument can also be used if you want async logging. 140 141 ```python 142 logger.add("somefile.log", enqueue=True) 143 ``` 144 145 Coroutine functions used as sinks are also supported and should be awaited with [`complete()`](https://loguru.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/logger.html#loguru._logger.Logger.complete). 146 147 ### Fully descriptive exceptions 148 149 Logging exceptions that occur in your code is important to track bugs, but it's quite useless if you don't know why it failed. """
Official test for NO_COLOR environment variable support.

import os
import pytest
from loguru import logger
from tests.conftest import StreamIsattyTrue, StreamIsattyFalse


def test_no_color_env_var_disables_auto_colorization():
    """Test that NO_COLOR disables automatic colorization for TTY streams."""
    old_no_color = os.environ.get('NO_COLOR')
    os.environ['NO_COLOR'] = '1'
    
    try:
        stream = StreamIsattyTrue()
        logger.remove()
        logger.add(stream, format="<green>{message}</green>", colorize=None)
        logger.info("Test message")
        
        output = stream.getvalue()
        assert '\x1b[' not in output  # No ANSI escape codes
        assert output == "Test message\n"
    finally:
        if old_no_color is None:
            os.environ.pop('NO_COLOR', None)
        else:
            os.environ['NO_COLOR'] = old_no_color


def test_no_color_env_var_disables_explicit_colorization():
    """Test that NO_COLOR overrides explicit colorize=True."""
    old_no_color = os.environ.get('NO_COLOR')
    os.environ['NO_COLOR'] = '1'
    
    try:
        stream = StreamIsattyTrue()
        logger.remove()
        logger.add(stream, format="<green>{message}</green>", colorize=True)
        logger.info("Test message")
        
        output = stream.getvalue()
        assert '\x1b[' not in output  # No ANSI escape codes
        assert output == "Test message\n"
    finally:
        if old_no_color is None:
            os.environ.pop('NO_COLOR', None)
        else:
            os.environ['NO_COLOR'] = old_no_color


def test_no_color_any_value_works():
    """Test that NO_COLOR works with any value including empty string."""
    test_values = ['', '0', '1', 'true', 'false', 'anything']
    
    for value in test_values:
        old_no_color = os.environ.get('NO_COLOR')
        os.environ['NO_COLOR'] = value
        
        try:
            stream = StreamIsattyTrue()
            logger.remove()
            logger.add(stream, format="<green>{message}</green>", colorize=None)
            logger.info("Test message")
            
            output = stream.getvalue()
            assert '\x1b[' not in output  # No ANSI escape codes
            assert output == "Test message\n"
        finally:
            if old_no_color is None:
                os.environ.pop('NO_COLOR', None)
            else:
                os.environ['NO_COLOR'] = old_no_color


def test_no_color_absent_allows_normal_behavior():
    """Test that absence of NO_COLOR allows normal color behavior."""
    # Ensure NO_COLOR is not set
    old_no_color = os.environ.get('NO_COLOR')
    if 'NO_COLOR' in os.environ:
        del os.environ['NO_COLOR']

        stream = StreamIsattyTrue()

    finally:
